paragraphs: High-school & college · Mathematics & physics
Patient, adaptive tutoring for students tackling difficult coursework, missing foundations, or an explanation that hasn’t clicked yet. You do not need to already be good at math to begin.
From algebra and geometry through advanced calculus and physics, build understanding at your own pace, with guidance that helps you solve problems independently.
In-Person Tutoring in Selected Washington, D.C., Maryland, and Virginia Areas | Online Nationwide
CONCEPT → CONNECTION → SOLUTION
Whether you’re a student working to catch up or a parent looking for thoughtful academic support, the starting point is what the student understands now.
Core expertise
Build the foundations, connect the ideas, and learn how to approach unfamiliar problems with a method.
Strengthen the prerequisite skills that make later mathematics more approachable.
Connect diagrams, relationships, and logical reasoning.
Understand the relationships behind trigonometric methods.
Build a connected foundation for the transition into calculus.
Connect rates of change and accumulation, from introductory to advanced undergraduate work.
Develop careful reasoning about data, uncertainty, and inference.
Connect mathematical reasoning to theory and physical application.
Beyond the core courses
Share your syllabus and the topics you need help with. Advanced undergraduate requests and graduate coursework are considered individually.
Teaching approach
A useful session goes beyond the answer to a single problem. The focus is on the concepts, decisions, and reasoning you can use on the next one.
Successful tutoring should eventually make the tutor unnecessary. The goal is understanding and independent problem-solving, with progressively less assistance.
Start with your questions. If you cannot identify what is confusing, work backward to what you do understand and find where the gap begins.
Repair missing prerequisites before moving forward. Adapt the explanation, examples, and pace to the student.
Connect theory to practice, then have the student work through problems with decreasing assistance.
Talk through the solution and test your understanding with guiding questions.
Identify patterns, practice a related problem, and decide what to work on next.
Meet your tutor
Learn about the teaching experience, mathematics education, and professional background behind each session.
Whether you’re seeking help for yourself or your student, bring your questions. We’ll start with what makes sense and build from there.

paragraphs: About your tutor
Get to know the background and experience behind the tutoring, and the belief that a clear explanation can change how a subject feels.
Academic profile
Advanced Math & Physics Tutor | Senior Software Engineer

A mathematics graduate of Stevens Institute of Technology with a minor in Physics, I bring approximately four years of prior tutoring experience and a professional background as a Senior Software Engineer, including Microsoft experience.
I enjoy the theory behind mathematics and the way physics puts it to work. My teaching is patient, analytical, and adapted to what each student needs to understand next.
Questions are encouraged. There is no expectation that you already understand the material.
Whether you’re seeking help for yourself or your student, bring your questions. We’ll start with what makes sense and build from there.

paragraphs: Sessions & policies
Know what to expect before you book, from the session format and rates to payment and cancellation policies.
The session experience
A focused 60-minute session, online nationwide through Google Meet or in person at one of four selected public locations.
Online sessions use a digital whiteboard and screen sharing. In-person sessions take place at the public location selected when booking.
Problem walkthroughs and conceptual explanations that connect the method to the underlying idea.
Exam review and homework clarification, with an emphasis on doing and understanding your own work.
Optional study planning, notes, or practice may be provided when useful. Recurring sessions are available; follow-up materials are not guaranteed after every session.
Rates vary by session format and location. View booking details for regular rates, promotional rates, and coupon codes.
Choose your format and location to see prices and the coupon to enter at Calendly checkout. Minimum booking: one 60-minute session.
Common questions
Find answers about getting started, preparing for a session, and managing your booking.

Primarily high-school students (including standard, honors, and AP courses) and college students. Mathematics, physics, engineering, and other majors taking quantitative courses are welcome. Graduate students are considered case-by-case.

Algebra, Geometry, Trigonometry, Precalculus, Calculus, Statistics, and Physics. Calculus coverage extends through Calculus III / Multivariable Calculus and Differential Equations. Advanced college mathematics requests can be discussed individually.

You do not need to already be good at math to work with me. Students who are struggling, failing, or missing prerequisites are welcome. We can work backward from what you understand to find and repair the foundational gap. Sometimes a different explanation or pace is what is needed.

Online tutoring is available nationwide through Google Meet, using screen sharing and a digital whiteboard. In-person tutoring meets at the four listed public locations in Winchester, Chantilly, Arlington, and Hanover. Contact support for help choosing a location. Online meeting details are provided through Calendly.

Whenever possible, email homework or problem sets, class notes, current topics, and the material causing difficulty. Include your attempted solutions and any upcoming exam topics so we can focus the session.

Yes. We can clarify concepts, identify errors, work through analogous problems, and prepare with permitted practice materials. You remain responsible for your own work. I do not complete graded assignments, provide answers to active graded examinations, or take quizzes or tests for students.

Notes or practice may be provided when useful, but are not guaranteed after every session. Occasional short questions by email are welcome; substantive instruction should generally wait until the tutoring session.

Sessions are 60 minutes. Rates vary by session format and location. View booking details for regular rates, promotional rates, and coupon codes. Minimum booking is one session. Enter the coupon shown for your selected option during Calendly checkout to receive its promotional rate.

Please give at least 24 hours’ notice to cancel or reschedule. Late cancellations and no-shows incur a charge of 50% of the session price. If I must cancel, you will not be charged; we can reschedule, and if a reasonable replacement time cannot be arranged, a full refund or credit will be provided.

I will generally provide the full 60 minutes when circumstances allow. The session may need to end at the originally scheduled time if another student is booked immediately afterward or an agreed public meeting location is closing.
Payment is due at booking and is collected through Calendly. Follow the payment steps in the booking calendar to complete your reservation.
Yes, recurring sessions are available. Email support to discuss a regular time. Availability at your selected public location must be confirmed.
